1.title: Audits, Assessments and Security Awareness
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty: Audits, Assessments and Security Awareness. It covers the exam area Security Program Management and Oversight. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. five point five Explain concepts associated with audit and assessment activities. five point six Given a scenario, apply security awareness concepts to improve organizational security. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Security Program Management and Oversight (fourteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: Audits and assessments
1.text: Audits and assessments. Audit. A formal, independent examination against a standard or policy. Assessment. An evaluation of controls or risk, often less formal. Gap analysis. Compare current state with the target to find missing controls. Benchmarking. Compare against peers or a standard.

1.title: Data gathering
1.text: Data gathering. Sampling (check part of the population), questionnaires and surveys, interviews, assertion (a statement by management that something is true), and reference sources such as. my ter attack. A catalog of attacker tactics and techniques. Cyber Kill Chain. Stages of an attack (reconnaissance to actions on objectives). Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis. Relates adversary, capability, infrastructure and victim.

1.title: Scoping and engagement types
1.text: Scoping and engagement types. Audit charter. The document that gives the audit authority and scope. Frequency. How often audits take place. Internal. Compliance checks, audit committee, self-assessments. External. Examinations, assessments, regulatory audits, independent third-party audits.

1.title: Scoping and engagement types, continued
1.text: Scoping and engagement types. The figure shows this: Internal and external audits compared by independence and who performs them. Exam tip: External independent audits give the most objective assurance. Self-assessments are the least independent. A gap analysis compares today versus the standard.

1.title: Penetration testing
1.text: Penetration testing. A penetration test is an authorized, simulated attack to find weaknesses. Always agree rules of engagement and get written permission first. Known environment (white box). Tester has full information. Unknown environment (black box). Tester has no information. Partially known environment (gray box). Some information. Physical. Tests buildings and locks. Offensive. The red team attacks. Defensive. The blue team defends and detects. Integrated. Red and blue work together (purple). Reconnaissance. Passive (public information, no contact with the target) or active (probing the target). Other topics: frameworks and standards (industry, international and region-specific), functional testing (does it do what it should), behavioral testing (how it behaves under unusual input).

1.title: Penetration testing, continued
1.text: Penetration testing. The figure shows this: Penetration test types by knowledge: known, partially known, unknown. Exam tip: Passive recon equals no contact (search engines, public records). Active recon equals touches the target (port scan). Unknown environment equals black box. Never test without written authorization.

1.title: Security awareness
1.text: Security awareness. Types of training. Initial or onboarding, ongoing, targeted (by role or risk), corrective (after a failure, for example a phishing click). Delivery mechanisms. Learning management system (L M S), self-service portals, one-to-one, one-to-many. Reporting and monitoring effectiveness. Metrics, managerial reports, personnel behavior risk scoring. Common topics. Social engineering, emerging security topics, password and credential management, remote work and hybrid work, B Y O D, business email compromise (B E C), removable media and cables, situational awareness, operational security. Measuring success: phishing simulation click rates, reporting rates, training completion, and incident trends. Reward reporting, do not punish it.

1.title: Security awareness, continued
1.text: Security awareness. The figure shows this: A phishing simulation cycle: send, measure, retrain, report. Exam tip: B E C is an email fraud where an attacker impersonates an executive or vendor to move money. Corrective training follows a failure. Targeted training matches high-risk roles (finance, executives).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors hires a firm to test its network. The testers are given no information about the environment. Which type is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Unknown environment. Testers with no prior information perform an unknown environment (black box) test.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A tester searches public records and social media about the company before any contact with its systems. Which activity is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Passive reconnaissance. Collecting information without touching the target is passive reconnaissance.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An employee clicks a link in a simulated phishing email. What should the company do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Provide corrective training. Corrective training addresses a failure, and the goal is learning rather than punishment.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which audit gives the most objective view for a regulator? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An independent third-party audit. Independent third-party audits are the most objective.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team compares its controls with the standard it wants to meet and lists what is missing. Which activity is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Gap analysis. A gap analysis compares the current state with the target to find gaps.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An attacker poses as the C E O and emails the finance team to change a vendor's bank account. Which threat does training cover here? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Business email compromise. Impersonating an executive by email to redirect payments is business email compromise.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does my ter attack provide? Answer: A catalog of attacker tactics and techniques. Question two. What is the difference between passive and active reconnaissance? Answer: Passive uses public information with no contact; active probes the target. Question three. Which penetration test type gives the tester full information? Answer: Known environment.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the four types of security awareness training? Answer: Initial or onboarding, ongoing, targeted and corrective. Question five. What is B E C? Answer: Business email compromise: impersonating executives or vendors to move money. Question six. What does an audit charter define? Answer: The authority and scope of an audit.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Audits: internal (compliance, audit committee, self-assessment) and external (regulatory, independent third party); gap analysis; benchmarking. Reference models: my ter attack, Cyber Kill Chain, Diamond Model. Pen testing: known, unknown, partially known; physical, offensive, defensive, integrated; passive versus active recon; written authorization. Awareness: initial, ongoing, targeted, corrective; L M S and portals; metrics and risk scoring. In the next module, we continue the course.
